meta.captureRoot: uktowns2/data + ukscotland/data (every UK capture either agent read, plus the fit14 extras)
meta.luptReference: fit14/lupt_fi.json, independently validated: 0 mismatches on all 181 days of the six captured LUPT months, and 365/365 fajr + 361/365 isha on the ELM capture
method: printed F = sunrise - fajr and I = isha - maghrib, day by day
implied twilight depression at the printed minute (NOAA solar position, cross-checked against adhan to 0.0 min)
core window Nov-Feb: the window where a 15-18 deg twilight exists at every UK latitude held, so a summer cap or an invented summer value cannot enter the verdict
constancy measured as observed jitter divided by the local rate of change, so a true angle rounded to the minute scores about 1 and a stepping table scores far higher
recipe naming at zero offset only: a free offset proves the angle form, never the recipe

thresholds.angle: a named angle reproduces the print at zero offset on >=95% of core days, or the implied depression is flat within the rounding floor
thresholds.interval: no angle holds the core print, and the implied depression swings >=2.5x the rounding floor, or the F/I array is constant
thresholds.undecidable: on a one-month span, no census angle holds and the jitter sits between 1.5x and 2.5x the floor

claims.fit4_restated: The English-Hanafi towns are one recipe FORM instantiated locally, but the form is not universal. Of 30 UK towns, 18 run a date-indexed interval table and 12 run an angle. Even inside the interval family the four fit4 towns split: Coventry and Bolton are LUPT plus a constant offset, Reading and Rochdale are their own arrays. The universal clause is what fails, not the form.
claims.fit12_restated: The modal form is the sunrise-anchored interval at 18 of 30 towns, the six-family map survives as an encoding-level description but not as a model-class one, because three of its members (Watford, Leicester, Blackpool, Stockport) are angles, and its isha "angle near 15" column is a free-offset artefact on the one-month prints: at zero offset a 15 deg isha hits 0 to 3 of 30 days at those towns.
claims.verify3_restated: The refutation holds and widens: Nottingham is one of 12 angle towns, not a lone counterexample, and the interval towns are 18 of 30 rather than all of them. The modal form holds, the universal does not.
claims.vocabulary: fit14 labels distance from LUPT, not model class. "drift" and "offset" can be true of an angle town (Watford +23, Leicester +24, Blackpool +11, Stockport +7 are all angles) because one month of an isha cannot separate the two. Any offset encoding read off a one-month print is model-agnostic.

bytes.note: F and I are 366 one-byte minutes each. Every capture as a full pair is 35 x 732 = 25.6 KB, and every town as a pair is 30 x 732 = 21.5 KB. Encoding only the table sides is 28 x 366 bytes plus the 732-byte LUPT base and about 60 parameter bytes.
